summary.text: A male infant was born with a complete bilateral cleft lip, alveolus, and palate, with the premaxilla distally rotated and intruded into the left nostril. Within 30 minutes of birth oral impressions were taken with an intraoral scanner, a digital alignment simulation was done, and a thermoplastic resin feeding plate was fabricated and fitted before the first feeding the same day.

The premaxilla achieved near midline alignment within 1 day of plate use. At 1 week of age a nasal stent was applied and soft resin added, with elastic lip tape, weekly resin adjustments and lateral expansion every 3 weeks. Lip repair was performed at 3 months of age, followed by palatoplasty at 12 months.

The upper lip achieved sufficient length, a normal anterior overbite was observed, and the premaxilla aligned without horizontal collapse. The nasal septum, initially curved at 1 month of age, was almost straightened by 2 months of age, and the authors state the septum was straightened at the time of palatoplasty in all cases.

summary.text: A male infant was born with a forward-protruding and left-deviated premaxilla, part of the series of bilateral cleft lip and palate cases. Because of the nocturnal delivery an intraoral scan was performed, followed by fabrication of a Hotz-type feeding plate based on a premaxillary alignment model.

At age 16 days a nasal stent was added and soft resin applied to the labial and occlusal surfaces of the premaxilla. Two elastic lip tapes were used to begin alignment, soft resin was added weekly, and premaxillary alignment was completed by age 2 months. Lip repair, continued Hotz-type plate use for the palatal cleft width, lateral expansion every 3 weeks and palatoplasty followed; the surgery ages differ between text and figure.

Palatoplasty resulted in sufficient upper lip length and a normal anterior overbite, and premaxillary alignment was achieved without horizontal collapse. The nasal septum, initially curved until 4 months of age, was almost straightened before palatoplasty; the authors also state that nasal septal curvature followed posterior premaxillary movement and the septum was straightened at palatoplasty in all cases.

summary.text: A female infant was born with a complete bilateral cleft lip, alveolus, and palate. An intraoral scan was performed immediately after birth and a Hotz-type feeding plate was fabricated. A nasal stent was applied at age 12 days, followed by soft resin on the labial and occlusal surfaces of the premaxilla, and two elastic lip tapes were used to initiate premaxillary alignment.

Weekly resin adjustments were made to achieve premaxillary alignment by 2 months, and the abstract states alignment was completed within 1 through 2 months of appliance placement in all 3 cases. Lip repair was performed at 3 months with continued Hotz-type plate use for the palatal cleft width, lateral expansion every 3 weeks, and palatoplasty at 12 months.

Palatoplasty resulted in sufficient upper lip length and an adequate overbite. The authors state that in all 3 cases nasal septal curvature was observed after posterior premaxillary movement and that the nasal septum was straightened at the time of palatoplasty in all cases.

figures.caption_summary: Clinical timeline of premaxilla-guiding nasoalveolar molding (PG-NAM) therapy in case 1. Sequential frontal and intraoral photographs documenting the course of PG-NAM therapy from birth through 13 months. Treatments included lip taping (until 3 months), Hotz-type feeding plate (until 12 months), PG-NAM appliance (until 3 months), and periodic labial or occlusal resin build-up (until 2 months). Primary lip repair was performed at 3 months, followed by palatoplasty at 12 months.

article_limitations: Case 2 text and Figure 5 caption disagree on lip repair (3 vs 4 months) and palatoplasty (12 vs 11 months); only the ages are review-only, the procedures stay included untimed, and the lip repair before palatoplasty order (agreed by both) is kept.
Case 2 text gives the intraoral scan at 16 hours after birth while the Figure 6 caption labels the birth model "at birth (1 hour)"; treated as a time-only source conflict (both sides review only).
The Discussion calls all 3 cases UCLP although the cases are described as bilateral; no fact is recorded from the UCLP wording.

Case 2 cleft-type wording appears only in the case heading, which is not part of the paragraph text and cannot be quoted; the cleft diagnosis for case 2 rests on the article-level statement that all 3 cases are BCLP.
Protocol-level statements ("PG-NAM is applied within 4 through 24 hours of birth", methods and discussion text, "in many cases of ultraearly initiation") are not copied to individual cases.

Figures 1 and 2 do not name a case and are not attributed to a patient; Figures 3 to 8 are attributed by their captions. No plot estimates are recorded; printed time labels in figures are pixel content in visual.json only.
